## Let's start!
Awesome, now you know everything you need to know about how to write a good
plugin for Fastify! After you have built one (or more!) let us know! We will add
it to the [ecosystem](https://github.com/fastify/fastify#ecosystem) section of
our documentation!

If you want to see some real world examples, check out:
- [`@fastify/view`](https://github.com/fastify/point-of-view) Templates
  rendering (*ejs, pug, handlebars, marko*) plugin support for Fastify.
- [`@fastify/mongodb`](https://github.com/fastify/fastify-mongodb) Fastify
  MongoDB connection plugin, with this you can share the same MongoDB connection
  pool in every part of your server.
- [`@fastify/multipart`](https://github.com/fastify/fastify-multipart) Multipart
  support for Fastify.
- [`@fastify/helmet`](https://github.com/fastify/fastify-helmet) Important
  security headers for Fastify.

## Let's start! Awesome, now you know everything you need to know about Fastify and its plugin system to start building your first plugin, and please if you do, tell us! We will add it to the [*ecosystem*](https://github.com/fastify/fastify#ecosystem) section of our documentation! If you want to see some real-world examples, check out: - [`@fastify/view`](https://github.com/fastify/point-of-view) Templates rendering (*ejs, pug, handlebars*) plugin support for Fastify. - [`@fastify/mongodb`](https://github.com/fastify/fastify-mongodb) Fastify MongoDB connection plugin, with this you can share the same MongoDB connection pool in every part of your server. - [`@fastify/multipart`](https://github.com/fastify/fastify-multipart) Multipart support for Fastify - [`@fastify/helmet`](https://github.com/fastify/fastify-helmet) Important security headers for Fastify *Do you feel like something is missing here? Let us know! :)*

request.instructions: The documents are sections of the documentation of ONE open-source project at one commit. Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).
